newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: About 5,000 workers strike at Northam.
newsitem.headline: About 5,000 workers strike at Northam.

text.p: About 5,000 mineworkers have gone on strike at Northam Platinum Ltd, mine managers Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd said on Friday.
A Gold Fields spokesman said that the strike over 1996/7 wages increases began on Thursday night when the night shift did not go underground.
The majority of Northam's National Union of Mineworkers members voted to strike last week after management and the union deadlocked over wages on September 26.
In a meeting on Monday, management met all the demands which the NUM had previously made at a conciliation board, Gold Fields said.
The union had initially demanded a 15 percent pay hike but was prepared to accept management's offer of 10 percent.
The company also said that it met the union's demand for additional quarterly increases aimed at reaching parity with wages paid on gold mines of the Gold Fields group.
It added that management's demand that the quarterly increases be conditional on profits being earned was dropped.
"The NUM made no further demands but mass meetings of workers held on Monday and Thursday evenings apparently rejected management's offer," the company said.
Northam produced 75,365 ounces of precious metals in concentrates in the three months to September.
The mine recorded a net loss before capital spending of 7.39 million rand in the September quarter after turning in a profit of 8.17 million in the previous quarter.
